sections.h2: Where is Greeley and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Greeley sits on the High Plains of northern Colorado, about 49 miles north-northeast of the State Capitol in Denver, and it is the county seat of Weld County. It is also the most populous municipality in the county.

The city covers a little over 49 square miles at an elevation of 4,676 feet. The Cache la Poudre River runs through the north side, and the South Platte River marks the southern edge of the wider Greeley and Evans area. Evans and Garden City border the city on the south. US 85 and US 34 are the two main highways serving it.

For a seller, two rivers and open farmland on the edges mean a house's location within the city can shape its story. A home near the river corridors and a home on the farmland edge are exposed to different conditions, and a buyer will ask about both.

sections.h2: How did Greeley start, and what does that history mean for older homes?
sections.html:
Greeley began in 1869 as the Union Colony, a planned farming community led by Nathan Meeker with the backing of New York Tribune editor Horace Greeley. The colonists bought 12,000 acres where the Cache la Poudre and South Platte rivers meet, and about 500 people had arrived by May of that year.

The town was incorporated on November 15, 1885. Telephones reached Greeley by 1883 and electric lights downtown by 1886, so the oldest blocks near the center carry well over a century of building history.

If you own a house on one of those older blocks, a traditional buyer's inspection can turn up repair requests on wiring, plumbing and the structure. A buyer who works with cash and buys as-is does not ask you to fix those items first.

The largest employer in Greeley is JBS USA, followed by Banner Health's North Colorado Medical Center and the Greeley-Evans School District 6. The city's own list of top employers, as of May 1, 2023, is summarized below.

Meatpacking, healthcare, education and government anchor the local job base. Hensel Phelps Construction and Atmos Energy's Colorado and Kansas operations are also based in the city, and Leprino Foods opened a cheese plant there that finished its final phase in 2017.

A household that depends on one of these employers may need to relocate on short notice for a transfer, a layoff or a new job in another state. When that happens, the closing date matters more than the last few thousand dollars of price.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Greeley, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Greeley has a semi-arid climate with hot summers, cold winters and very low humidity. Summer highs usually run around 90 to 95 degrees Fahrenheit, and winter highs sit around 40 to 45 degrees. The first freeze typically arrives near October 4 and the last near May 4.

Hail is the big concern for roofs. The farmland around Greeley sees roughly 7 to 9 hail days a year, according to the climate summary on the city's Wikipedia entry. On May 28, 2024, a severe hailstorm hit the east side of the city, covering some areas in more than a foot of hail. The mayor signed a local disaster declaration, and officials put city damage at more than $1.45 million.

If your roof took hail damage and you never filed or finished an insurance claim, that matters when you sell. A traditional buyer's inspector will flag it, and a lender may ask for repairs. Cash buyers price the roof into the offer instead of requiring you to replace it first.

  • Ask your insurer whether a hail claim is still open or can still be filed.
  • Keep invoices for any roof, gutter or window work already done.
  • Photograph damage you have not repaired before you list or request an offer.

sections.h2: Which schools, colleges and hospitals serve Greeley?
sections.html:
Most of Greeley and neighboring Evans fall inside Greeley-Evans School District 6. The district runs elementary, K-8, middle, junior high and high school campuses, including Greeley West, Greeley Central and Northridge high schools, and it also oversees several charter schools.

Higher education adds steady rental demand. The University of Northern Colorado enrolls about 9,000 students, and Aims Community College also has a campus in the city. Healthcare is anchored by North Colorado Medical Center, which opened in 1904, and by UCHealth Greeley Hospital, which opened in 2019.

With thousands of students and staff at the university and the community college, rental housing is part of the local picture. An owner who wants out of a rental can sell with or without the tenant in place.

sections.h2: How do people get around Greeley?
sections.html:
Greeley is driven more than it is ridden, but there are transit and air options. The local bus agency, formerly Greeley-Evans Transit and rebranded as Gallop in 2026, runs seven local routes. Gallop also operates the Poudre Express, a regional bus that connects Greeley with Windsor and Fort Collins.

Express Arrow buses run to Denver, and the Greeley-Weld County Airport handles local air traffic. US 34 and US 85 are the highways that link the city to the rest of the Front Range.

sections.h2: What will I owe in property tax when I sell a Greeley house?
sections.html:
Weld County bills property tax in arrears, so the tax you pay in a given year covers the prior year. The Weld County Treasurer's published 2026 schedule shows a first half due February 28, a second half due June 15 and a full payment option due April 30.

Payment option2026 due date (Weld County)
First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Notices are normally mailed before the end of January to the owner of record. Partial payments are not accepted, and a bill of $25 or less must be paid in a single payment. Payments postmarked late pick up interest that starts at 1 percent in March for a first half and climbs month by month.

Your mortgage company does not get a copy of the tax notice from the treasurer. If a lender pays from escrow, the treasurer processes that payment and returns yours if both arrive. The treasurer's office also publishes a request form for a Certificate of Taxes Due, which is the document a closing needs to show what is owed on the parcel. You can read the details on the Weld County Treasurer page.

Name changes follow a recorded deed. The assessor updates ownership only after the deed is recorded with the Weld County Clerk and Recorder, so a seller should make sure the closing company records promptly.

sections.h2: What steps does a Greeley sale follow, and where do cash sales differ?
sections.html:
A Greeley sale has the same basic steps as any Colorado sale, and a cash purchase simply removes several of them. The list below shows where time is usually lost.

  • Listing with an agent adds weeks for photos, showings, offers, the buyer's inspection and the appraisal.
  • Financed buyers can fall through when an appraisal comes in low or underwriting stalls.
  • A cash purchase can skip the appraisal and loan approval, so closing can be set around your move date.
  • Either way, a title company handles the deed, the tax certificate and the recording with Weld County.

We buy Greeley houses in the condition they are in, including houses with hail-damaged roofs, tenants, deferred maintenance or probate paperwork still open. You decide whether the offer works, and there is no obligation to accept it.

sections.h2: What do Greeley sellers most often face?
sections.html:
Greeley sellers most often contend with storm damage, older plumbing and electrical, tenants in place and inherited property. Each one slows a retail listing.

  • Roof and exterior wear from hail seasons.
  • Rentals with tenants in place and deferred upkeep.
  • Estates where heirs live out of state and want one closing instead of months of upkeep.
  • Owners relocating for work after a change at a large local employer.

If your situation looks like one of these, tell us about the property and we will respond with a straightforward offer or a clear reason we cannot make one.

faqs.a: Yes. Greeley is the county seat of Weld County and its most populous municipality, so deeds are recorded with the Weld County Clerk and Recorder and property tax is billed by the Weld County Treasurer.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Greeley?
faqs.a: Weld County's published 2026 deadlines are February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for a single full payment. Late postmarks add interest, so check the treasurer's page for the current year.

faqs.q: Does hail damage hurt my chances of selling a Greeley house?
faqs.a: It can, because inspectors and lenders flag damaged roofs. Greeley's farmland surroundings see several hail days a year, and a major storm in May 2024 hit the east side hard. A cash buyer can account for roof condition in the offer instead of asking you to repair it first.

faqs.q: Who are the largest employers near Greeley?
faqs.a: As of May 1, 2023, the city's list put JBS USA first with 5,141 employees, followed by Banner Health's North Colorado Medical Center with 4,558 and Greeley-Evans School District 6 with 2,258.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greeley house with tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us about the lease and the rent, and we will include the tenancy in the offer. You do not need to empty the house or finish repairs first.
